scope: Additive native-only source-character text revision capture with an explicit RejectInterveningText policy. Complete original joined/protected general-range semantics, source-inherited insertion formats, fresh floors, original scope and conservative child guards are retained. This is not the preserving-peer-insertions policy or paired client delivery; the full advanced-review goal remains active.
laws: The current observation is checked before untrusted bytes. A complete original source effect is evaluated on a disposable native fork; missing source operations remain Pending. Malformed source intents, no source effect and normal resource/namespace limits reject without live mutation.

Selected original scalars must survive in order in the same protected domain and text kind. Complete source/current marks on those originals must match. Equal-looking deletion/reinsertion is character loss, not a usable replacement. Unselected text and marks can change without forcing the old whole-text-block guard onto this explicit revision.

Every selected original segment must lie inside the mapped range, and its total UTF-16 length must equal current native coverage. Otherwise RejectInterveningText reports a conflict rather than deleting a peer insertion or applying a surviving subset. Headers, whole atoms and structural contexts retain native source witnesses; whole images/tables cannot be silently removed after modification.

Collapsed original insertions remain collapsed at their directional anchor's mapped affinity, even if their Before/After endpoints now surround newly typed text. Plain InsertText recovers the exact source-inherited rich runs from its proved original native effect instead of inheriting current foreign marks.

A captured child keeps original creator and explicit scope and uses the existing general planner for joins, preserved partial structures, whole-atom deletion and exact fresh floors. A two-by-twenty-cell case requires 38 fresh empty paragraphs and stays one declarative GeneralText intent instead of being cut down to the 64-command ceiling. Repeated children remain rebased declarative intents before acceptance.

Capture remains pure in read-only mode with retained Redo. Under all six layout-V3 selection/history policies, exact source/frame/view and future history survive capture and native reopen. The old original proposal still conflicts after a disjoint block edit; its saved meaning is not weakened.

The authenticated reference host supersedes the original pending proposal separately from Accept. Across all six policies, Accept preserves peer prefix/suffix text and unrelated marks, supplies once-only accepting-writer history, recovers exact Undo/Redo and returns the original decision after host restart and lease renewal without another append.

Direct local own-writer GeneralText effect commit still requires its existing explicit general-history family. Pure proposal capture and authenticated server-owned acceptance are available to original, general and document source-history families. No existing mutation factory or recovery family is silently enabled.

bounds.note: Existing source, schema, structural/floor, revision-envelope and historical-cut budgets also apply. No partial child, plain fallback, native identity regeneration or automatic namespace reuse is introduced.

verificationNotes: Canonical tests cover stale-observation precedence, pending source recovery, changed selected formats, intervening text refusal, equal reinsertion, structural witness changes, collapsed affinities, source-inherited formats, repeated children, explicit Document scope, joined atom removal with exact local Undo/Redo, protected tables/captions, wide native floors and pure read-only capture under all six policies. The compatibility target runs the same source file, not a fork.

The direct local-effect regression initially attempted GeneralText commit in an original-only own-writer history and correctly received the existing general semantic history required refusal. That regression now explicitly enables and restores the general family. The separate server-owned acceptance regression still passes all six original/general/document and explicit/natural combinations.

An initial relay lint failure for a long test function was repaired with named capture/acceptance helpers, without adding a lint suppression. The pinned engine's existing HasIdSpan unused-import warning remains unchanged.

These are native Rust and durable reference-host results, not new Wasm, SDK, toolbar, browser, IME or accessibility evidence. Source applications have no new text-rebase runtime capability at this checkpoint. The earlier asset-backed installed checkpoint remains separate evidence for the already delivered review features.

remaining: An identity-preserving masked replacement policy for peer characters inserted inside the original replacement, including explicit joined/protected structural consequences. No product default has been selected. Copying and reinserting peer text is not an equivalent implementation.

Paired optional text-rebase Wasm/SDK capability, durable revision-outbox integration, borrowed vanilla/React controls and clean-installed mixed acceptance. Mixed command-batch text rebasing remains explicitly unsupported rather than partially executed.
